rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited challenge that the Creator of heaven and earth can create their likeness supports the claim that God can raise the dead.
rows.anchor: أو ليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death and life are paired and dependent: if a second death had no following life, it would be extinction rather than death in its proper sense.
rows.anchor: الموت والحياة مزدوجان متضايفان , وإذا استوفى الموت الأول إحياؤه فلا بد من استيفاء الموت الثاني إحياؤه أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is a transient hidden beginning before manifestation, while life is an enduring, established end; mortality passes and life remains.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الموت حال غيب بين يديه ظهور , والحياة نهاية ثابتة , والموت مبدأ غيب زائل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Biqai cites as sound a Prophetic report that death will be slaughtered, signaling the end of death as a kind and the permanence of life.
rows.anchor: ورد ما صح عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام في أن الموت يذبح , إعلام بانقضاء جنسه وثبات الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording in 67:2 mentions death before life because the definite article encompasses both kinds, with life following death in the wording.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قدم في الذكر وأعقب بالحياة حيث استغرقتهما كلمة ( أل ) في قوله :

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Biqai cites the Prophet’s statement that the bliss of Paradise has no end; no grading is stated for this report.
rows.anchor: كما ورد عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : ( نعيم الجنة لا آخر له )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second revival raises people after burial and the barzakh, restoring their former capacity to move by the power that first created and caused them to die.
rows.anchor: فينشركم بعد طيكم ويبعثكم بعد حبسكم في البرزخ ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of resurrection does not rule out that people have some awareness in the barzakh before receiving their complete bodily form.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا ينفي أن يكون لهم في البرزخ إحساس بدون هذه الهيئة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is a gathering after a long standing for recompense through reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: فيحشركم بعد طول الوقوف للجزاء من الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says those who do not return voluntarily through worldly knowledge will be compelled after resurrection, when their supposed helpers and objects of worship fail them, and then judged.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحرالي : إعلام بأنهم إن لم يرجعوا إلى الله سبحانه بداعي العلم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai identifies 2:281 as the last verse revealed: it is the final address encompassing all who face judgment, with no later comprehensive statement beyond it.
rows.anchor: وهذا آخر خطاب الإقبال عليهم من دعوة الله لهم ولسان النكير عليهم , ولذلك كانت آية :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return means that a thing comes back to its point of origin when it reaches the end of its course.
rows.anchor: والرجع عود الشيء عند انتهاء غايته إلى مبدئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai says the verse unpacks the earlier summary of human beginnings, middle, and end: creation is an act of favor that calls people to God through proof of power and kindness that elicits love.
rows.anchor: ليكون داعيا إلى توحيده من وجهين : كونه دالا على عظمة مؤثرة وكمال قدرته ,

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali reads “He” as pointing to the transcendent unseen God who sustains everything; the divine essence remains hidden while the names disclose Him.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهي كلمة مدلولها العلي غيب الإلهية القائم بكل شيء الذي لا يظهر لشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address warns persistent disbelievers after promising their return, using a threat that may draw them back willingly or by force.
rows.anchor: قال : لما انتهى الخطاب بذكر إرجاعهم إلى الله وكان هذا خطابا خاصا مع المتمادي على كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is like a slack rope that may draw a person back through divine kindness or pull him forcibly at the end of his turning away.
rows.anchor: قال : لما انتهى الخطاب بذكر إرجاعهم إلى الله وكان هذا خطابا خاصا مع المتمادي على كفره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the ending of the call echoes its opening, though this verse sharply separates its two ends by moving from the unseen divine name to tangible earthly creation.
rows.anchor: وانتظم به ختم آية الدعوة بنحو من ابتدائها , إلا أن هذه على نهاية الاقتطاع بين طرفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created what is on earth for people as a kindness to them in both their religious and worldly lives.
rows.anchor: { الذي خلق لكم } دينا ودنيا لطفا بكم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says “all” signals that human needs depend on the whole of earthly creation; losing one element causes others to falter.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وقوله : { جميعا } إعلان بأن حاجة الإنسان لا تقوم بشيء دون شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that created things are presumptively permissible; nothing is prohibited without evidence.
rows.anchor: والآية دليل على أن الأصل في الأشياء الإباحة , فلا يمنع شيء إلا بدليل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elevated heaven, firm construction, ordered beauty, and many benefits warrant the connective “then,” which magnifies its rank.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت السماء أشرف من جهة العلو الذي لا يرام , والجوهر البالغ في الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned His will toward arranging the heaven, whose height, beauty, purity, and abundant benefits are emphasized.
rows.anchor: ثم علق إرادته ومشيئته بتسويتها من غير أدنى عدول ونظر إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Harali notes that heaven is where people fear harmful events will descend, so the verse reassures them that God governs the very realm they fear.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : أعلى الخطاب بذكر الاستواء إلى السماء الذي هو موضع التخوف لهم لنزول المخوفات منه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fitting sense of divine istiwāʾ concerns rank and unseen realities, not a restriction to bodily locations and sensory appearances.
rows.anchor: مجرى لفظ الاستواء في الرتبة والمكانة أحق بمعناه من موقعه في المكان والشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “heaven” can indicate the elevated direction or the heavenly kind; the following plural pronoun signals the seven individual heavens.
rows.anchor: الإفراد الصالح لجهة العلو تنبيها على الشرف , وللجنس الصالح للكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was created and prepared before the heaven, then spread out afterward; “then” can mark exaltation rather than sequence, and earth is mentioned first because it is closer to human experience.
rows.anchor: فكان خلق الأرض وتهيئتها لما يراد منها قبل خلق السماء , ودحوها بعد خلق السماء ؛ على أن ثم للتعظيم لا للترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse puts earth first because its close connection to human beings makes it a more immediate sign.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الأرض هنا لأنها أدل لشدة الملابسة والمباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the heavens even means giving each constituent its due so that the whole reaches its perfected form.
rows.anchor: التسوية إعطاء أجزاء الشيء حظه لكمال صورة ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai completes the implied benefit: everything in the heavens was also created for human use.
rows.anchor: وخلق جميع ما فيها لكم , فالآية من الاحتباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the rare figure of ḥatbāk: the seven earthly levels are omitted because the seven heavens indicate them, and heavenly benefits are omitted because earthly benefits already indicate them.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك ؛ حذف أولا كون الأراضي سبعا لدلالة الثاني عليه , وثانيا كون ما في السماء لنا لدلالة الأول عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered creation proves the maker’s power; since its arrangement rests on knowledge, the verse ends by naming knowledge and thereby affirms His power over all things.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الخلق على هذه الكيفية دالا بالبديهة على أتم قدرة لصانعه وكان العلم بأن مبنى ذلك على العلم محتاجا إلى تأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the visible cycles of life and death point to resurrection, the ordered cosmos and its knowledge-bearing close prepare the account of humanity’s creation and its gift of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر الحياة والموت المشاهدين تنبيها على القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of humanity’s beginning continues the command to worship the Lord and explains the description of God as Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: عطفا على قوله : { اعبدوا ربكم } وبيانا لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai outlines four aims of the surah’s discourse: show divine names, awaken hope and fear about the unseen end, recount God’s past acts to spur worship, and reveal the inward reality of the present.
rows.anchor: أحدها التنبيه على الآيات بمقتضى أسماء الله من اسمه الملك إلى اسمه الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali links the Adam account to the preceding stages of the surah: after categorizing people and issuing a general call beneath the veil of predestination, revelation now discloses the beginning of human creation.
rows.anchor: ثم أنزل الخطاب إلى آية الدعوة من وراء حجاب الستر بسابق التقدير فعم به الناس ونبههم على آيات ربوبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai reads Adam’s public creation story as a manifest sign concealing the more elevated, privately understood account of Muhammad’s creation.
rows.anchor: فذكر خلق آدم ظاهر خبء ما عطف عليه وهو والله أعلم ذكر خلق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord” is the benefactor who showed mercy to humanity through Muhammad and kept him concealed within the disclosure of Adam’s creation.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليك برحمة العباد بك الذي خبأك في إظهار خلق آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction wāw joins what follows to something stated or understood before it; idh is an ambiguous noun for a past event or time.
rows.anchor: فإن الواو حرف يجمع ما بعده مع شيء قبله إفصاحا في اللفظ أو إفهاما في المعنى , وإنما يقع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl is the outward arrangement of verbal forms, like the joining of visible forms; the heart apprehends speech through the ear as it apprehends visible things through sight.
rows.anchor: { قال } من القول وهو إبداء صور الكلم نظما بمنزلة ائتلاف الصور المحسوسة جمعا , فالقول مشهود القلب بواسطة الأذن

rows.speaker: أهل العربية
rows.claim: The grammarians derive malāʾika from the inverted form malāʾik, itself from maʾlak and the root of sending a message; on this account the mīm is extra.
rows.anchor: وتأويل الملائكة عند أهل العربية أنه جمع ملاك مقلوب من مألك من الألك وهي الرسالة ,

rows.speaker: أهل العربية
rows.claim: A second derivation connects malak to dominion and control, as in kneading dough, with an original mīm and the sense of shaping or ordering.
rows.anchor: ويكون الملك من الملك وهو إحكام ما منه التصوير , من ملكت العجين , وجمعه أملاك , تكون فيه الميم أصلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai proposes that malāʾika gathers both senses, messenger and ordering power, as a coined word can unite meanings from two roots.
rows.anchor: فليكن اسم ملائكة جامعا للمعنيين منحوتا من الأصلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai compares the blended derivation to insān, which he says carries both the senses of sociability and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: كثيرا ما يوجد ذلك في أسماء الذوات الجامعة كلفظ إنسان بما ظهر فيه من أنه من الأنس والنسيان معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai describes two levels of discourse, a general one and a higher, more particular one that yields increasingly elevated meanings.
rows.anchor: رتبة عامة ورتبة خاصة أفصح وأعلى كلما وكلاما . قال : وفيه أي هذا الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disclosure isolates discerning hearts in attachment to God alone: God gave Adam life without the angels, so hearts should not depend on any created favorite, preparing for the warning about following Satan.
rows.anchor: قال : وفيه أي هذا الخطاب مع ذلك استخلاص لبواطن أهل الفطانة من أن تعلق بواطنهم بأحد من دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai says every verse connects with what precedes and prepares for what follows; this coherence is part of the Qur’an’s inimitability.
rows.anchor: وبذلك كان انتظام الآي داخلا في معنى الإعجاز الذي لا يأتي الخلق بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna conveys emphasis grounded in the speaker’s own self and knowledge, while the first-person suffix marks attribution to oneself.
rows.anchor: { إني } إن حرف يفهم توكيدا من ذات نفس المؤكد وعلمه . والياء اسم علي يخص المضيف إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s succession extends across the earth through himself and his descendants; the singular khalīfa suits the completeness of this role, though it can also be generic.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت خلافة آدم عليه السلام كاملة في جميع الأرض بنفسه وبذريته وحد لذلك مع أنه يصح أن يراد به الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A khalīfa is one who carries out the predecessor’s work according to that deputy’s rank; humans succeed one another, while Adam is God’s deputy in the realm of dominion.
rows.anchor: الخليفة ذات قائم بما يقوم به المستخلف على حسب رتبة ذلك الخليفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder invites worship and love by recounting God’s favors before humanity existed: His defense of them before angels, Adam’s knowledge and honor, and His forgiveness of Adam despite expelling Iblis after his worship.
rows.anchor: فذكر لهم ما حاج به ملائكته عنهم , وما شرف به أباهم آدم من العلم وأمر الملائكة المقربين بالسجود له

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the discourse turns from God’s earlier direct address to the Israelites to the Prophet’s report of what Moses told them after their grave sin.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : لما تكمل إقبال الخطاب عليهم مرات بما تقدم من ندائهم والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God honors people by addressing them without an intermediary, while others receive His address through a prophet; the Israelites’ wrongdoing brought this mediated address.
rows.anchor: فإن الله يخاطب العباد بإسقاط الواسطة بينه وبينهم ترفيعا لأقدارهم لديه , فيرفع من شاء فيجيبه بما شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ people here are both those who worshiped the calf and those who remained silent about it.
rows.anchor: { وإذ قال موسى لقومه } العابد للعجل والساكت عنه ,

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali derives qawm from standing up to the task for which people are mentioned, contrasting the term with women because of their weakness in such efforts.
rows.anchor: والقوم قال الحرالي اسم من لهم منة في القيام بما هم مذكورون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns Muhammad’s community that disrespect in addressing God could bring the same consequence: God turning away from them.
rows.anchor: وفيه تخويف لهذه الأمة أن يصيبهم مثل ما أصابهم في خطاب ربهم فيعرض عنهم - انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calf worship was the worst injustice because people lowered themselves by submitting to an inferior object instead of God; one should not worship an equal, much less a lesser creature.
rows.anchor: فأنزلتموها من رتبة عزها بخضوعها لمولاها الذي لا يذل من والاه ولا يعز من عاداه إلى ذلها بخضوعها لمن هو دونكم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali ranks minerals below living plants: plants display life and provide nourishing or medicinal grain and fruit, while minerals serve only as tools or currency and benefit through being extracted.
rows.anchor: المعادن لا ينتفع بها إلا آلات ونقودا منفعتها إخراجها لا إثباتها - قاله الحرالي :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai explains the call to repent to the One who brought them into being before they made the calf, and whose creation gives them varied, well-formed shapes.
rows.anchor: الذي فطركم من قبل أن تتخذوا العجل بريئين من العيب مع إحكام الخلق على الأشكال المختلفة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines the Bāriʾ as the one who prepares and repairs materials for their intended form, like a tailor cutting cloth or a baker preparing grain.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : البارئ اسم قائم بمعنى البرء وهو إصلاح المواد للتصوير ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to kill yourselves refers to killing relatives, including parents or children; they are called selves because of kinship and to signal the gravity of their sin.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت توبتهم بقتل أقاربهم وإن كانوا آباء أو أبناء عبر عنهم بالنفس لذلك وإشارة إلى خبث ما ارتكبوا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines killing as cutting off an animal before its strength is spent, like cutting a crop before it ripens.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والقتل قصل الحيوان قبل انتهاء قوته بمنزلة قصل الزرع قبل استحصاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the severe killing command “better” magnifies the reward and encourages them to accept it despite its great difficulty.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ما أمرهم به أمرا لا يكاد يسمح به عظم الرغبة فيه بقوله { ذلكم } أي الأمر العظيم وهو القتل { خير لكم }

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says khayr can mean what is fit to choose or the most choiceworthy; without comparison it can mean something good in itself.
rows.anchor: والخير قال الحرالي ما يصلح في الاختيار من محسوس الأشياء وما هو الأصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInda expresses a broad relation such as possession, while ladun is more specific and implies presence.
rows.anchor: { عند } كلمة تفهم اختصاص ما أضيفت إليه بوجه ما عام وأخص منه لدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God your Bāriʾ reminds them that He can both create and annihilate them, combining encouragement through favor with warning of humiliation.
rows.anchor: { بارئكم } أي القادر على إعدامكم كما قدر على إيجادكم , وفي التعبير بالبارئ ترغيب لهم في طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgave them after they carried out the difficult repentance by killing one another; His pardon made their repentance possible despite their grave offense.
rows.anchor: ولما كان التقدير ففعلتم التوبة المأمور بها بأن قتل بعضكم بعضا بتوفيقه لكم سبحانه مع ما فيه من عظم المشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being ever-turning and merciful is an enduring attribute, not a response earned by the Israelites’ own merit.
rows.anchor: أي ما زال هذا صفة له لا لاستحقاق منكم عليه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the separate pronoun huwa affirms mercy as constant, though its manifestation lies beyond the hidden wisdom of discipline, trial, or punishment; ending with al-Raḥīm discloses the subtler meaning.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي إظهار هو مفصولة من ضمير وصلها إثبات معنى الرحمة لله ثبتا لا يتبدل ولا يتغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After clinging to the sensory calf, the Israelites demanded sensory sight of their Creator, forgetting His favors and signs; their story consoles Muhammad over his people’s rejection.
rows.anchor: ولما استتيبوا عن عبادة العجل التي تقيدوا فيها بالمحسوس الذي هو مثل في الغباوة طلبوا رؤية بارئهم بالحس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand came despite clear signs that should remove doubt; it reflects a rigid attachment to imagination and sense, a pattern also seen in Moses’ own people.
rows.anchor: والحال أن الفرقان الذي لا يدع شبهة ولا يبقى حيرة قائم بين أيديهم , لأنهم من الجمود والوقوف مع الوهم والحس بمكان عظيم ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Moses by his bare name, despite witnessing God honor him and honor them through him, shows their discourtesy and harshness.
rows.anchor: فدعوتموه باسمه جفاء وغلظة كما يدعو بعضكم بعضا ولم تخصوه بما يدل على تعظيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai points to 9:61 as a Qur’anic parallel where the lām construction “believe for the believers” differs from “believe in God.”
rows.anchor: 77 ( { يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This distinction explains that the Israelites accepted Moses’ basic message but stopped short of accepting the detailed matters he brought.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ḥattā marks a bounded endpoint that falls within the preceding condition’s scope, unlike the purposive particle kay.
rows.anchor: { حتى } كلمة تفهم غاية محوطة يدخل ما بعدها في حكم ما قبلها مقابل معنى لكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing is access to an inward reality through its visible outward aspect; dream vision presents inner realities in forms like waking sight.
rows.anchor: { نرى } من الرؤية وهي اطلاع على باطن الشيء الذي أظهر منه مبصره الذي أظهره منه منظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Allah here carries the sense of divine greatness, heightening the impropriety of their demand.
rows.anchor: { الله } أي مع ما له من العظمة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines jahr as public disclosure reaching notoriety and an audience not specifically selected, in contrast to a private communication for its intended recipient.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الجهر وهو الإعلان بالشيء إلى حد الشهرة وبلاغه لمن لا يقصد في مقابلة السر المختص بمن يقصد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public sight of God is an unsuitable demand: unveiling belongs to chosen people granted nearness, not those in a position of distance and rejection.
rows.anchor: وهذا المطلوب مما لا يليق بالجهر لتحقيق اختصاصه بمن يكشف له الحجاب من خاصة من يجوزه القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage points to Moses’ request to see God and to the radiant faces looking toward their Lord as scriptural language for this special vision.
rows.anchor: وفيه شهادة بتبلدهم عن موقع الرؤية , فإن موسى عليه السلام قال
